Multispecies false-positive occupancy model

Source: R/fp_occu_ms.R
fp_occu_ms.Rd

Fits the false-positive occupancy model of fp_occu() to several species at once, with the coefficients of each species drawn from distributions of the community, so that rare species borrow strength from the others. This function is in development (see crywolf-api): its arguments, results and output names may change in a minor version, and it lacks the methods of fp_occu() other than print(), summary() and as_draws_df().

Usage

fp_occu_ms(
  data,
  occ = ~1,
  det = ~1,
  fp = ~1,
  random_recorder = !is.null(data$recorder),
  ver = ~1,
  priors = fp_priors(),
  centered = FALSE,
  chains = 4,
  parallel_chains = chains,
  threads_per_chain = "auto",
  iter_warmup = 1000,
  iter_sampling = 1000,
  adapt_delta = 0.95,
  seed = NULL,
  refresh = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_ms'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_ms'
summary(object, prob = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_ms'
as_draws_df(x, ...)

Arguments

data

An fp_data object with a species column; see the species argument of fp_data().

occ, det, fp, random_recorder, ver, priors

As in fp_occu(). The standard deviations among species have the half-Normal priors of fp_priors(species_sd = ); the community means have the priors of the intercepts, slopes and gap of fp_priors().

centered

Use the centred parametrization of the detection intercepts, gaps and recorder effects? The model is the same. TRUE suits passive acoustic monitoring, with thousands of occasions per species: their posteriors are then so narrow that the default takes very small steps and reaches the maximum tree depth. Keep FALSE with few occasions per species or recorder.

chains, parallel_chains, threads_per_chain, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, adapt_delta, seed, refresh, ...

Passed to the sampler, as in fp_occu(). Runs of detections (markov) and site effects (random_fp, random_det) are not available.

x, object

An fp_occu_ms object.

digits

Number of digits to print.

prob

Width of the equal-tailed credible interval.

Value

An object of class fp_occu_ms, a list with fit, draws (readable names: see Details), stan_data, formulas, design, data, random_recorder, priors, sampler, diagnostics and call.

summary() returns an object of class summary.fp_occu, as for fp_occu().

Details

Each species \(s\) has its own occupancy coefficients \(\beta_s = \mu_\beta + \sigma_\beta z_s\) (all the terms of occ, with \(z_s\) standard normal), its own true-detection intercept \(\alpha_s = \alpha + \sigma_\alpha z_s\), and its own gap between the true-detection and false-positive intercepts, \(g_s = \mu_g \exp(\sigma_g z_s)\), which keeps the false-positive rate of every species below its true-detection rate at the reference. The slopes of det, fp and ver, the intercept of the verified method and the recorder effect are shared by the species. The false positives of a species are independent of those of the others: the classifier errs in labelling a species, not in confusing two species.

The species are those of the data (fp_data(species = )), and a species is never assumed to be absent from the list: there is no data augmentation for species never detected.

Output names. The community means have the names of fp_occu() (occ_*, det_*, fp_*, fp_gap, the median gap, and p11_ref, p10_ref at the community means); the standard deviations among species are sd_occ_*, sd_det_(Intercept) and sd_log_fp_gap; and the values of each species carry its name in brackets: occ_*[species], det_(Intercept)[species], fp_gap[species], p11_ref[species] and p10_ref[species].

See also

fp_data(), fp_occu()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# name every species to keep (`schema.json` lists them)
x <- fp_read_sheepdog("occupancy_export",
                      species = c("ela_bic", "lep_fus", "phy_cuv"))
d <- fp_draws_data(x, n_draws = 1)[[1]]
m <- fp_occu_ms(d, fp = ~ 1)
m
} # }
